objects.name: Apple
objects.notes: Universally recognized fruit silhouette.

objects.name: Pear
objects.notes: Slightly lower cross-cultural familiarity than apple; kept as the apple/pear hard-tier distractor pair per spec, low ambiguity risk.

objects.name: Cup
objects.notes: Tapered drinking glass silhouette, distinct from mug's handle.

objects.name: Mug
objects.notes: Straight-walled vessel with handle; intentional near-match to cup for hard-tier discrimination.

objects.name: Pen
objects.notes: Smooth barrel with cap ring, distinguishes from pencil's tip hatching.

objects.name: Pencil
objects.notes: Faceted barrel with sharpened-tip hatch marks; intentional near-match to pen.

objects.name: Fork
objects.notes: Moderate cultural-neutrality caveat: fork is not the primary eating utensil in all cultures (chopstick- and hand-eating traditions), but is broadly visually recognized worldwide via global product exposure. Kept per original spec's explicit fork/spoon example; flagged for awareness, not replaced.

objects.name: Spoon
objects.notes: Near-universal utensil across virtually all cultures; intentional near-match to fork.

objects.name: Clock

objects.name: Bottle

objects.name: Scissors

objects.name: Wallet

objects.name: Glasses
objects.notes: Universal, and specifically high-familiarity for the older-adult target population. Paired with sunglasses below for hard-tier discrimination.

objects.name: Backpack
